answer: A farm scripting its whole swarm fires them together, so that the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 14 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. The sparrow detector writes to velvet, and timber makes public every merge. Submissions that land within 40 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 37 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
